questions.q: What is the primary definition of a constitution in a democratic country?
questions.a: A constitution is the supreme legal document that establishes the structure of government, distributes powers among its branches, and guarantees rights to citizens. A wrong answer—such as thinking it is merely a history textbook or a list of daily government orders—reveals a confusion between ordinary laws/historical events and fundamental, supreme law.

questions.q: Why is a constitution referred to as the "supreme law of the land"?
questions.a: It is supreme because all other laws, policies, and actions of the government must comply with it; any ordinary law that contradicts the constitution is invalid. A wrong answer suggests that the student believes the current ruling party or Parliament can pass any law they want without any legal restrictions or higher authority.

questions.q: If Parliament passes a law that bans citizens from practicing their religion, how does the constitution protect citizens?
questions.a: The constitution acts as a shield by enshrining fundamental rights that limit government power; any law violating these constitutional guarantees is struck down by the judiciary. A wrong answer indicates the student thinks the government has absolute, unchecked power over the people.

questions.q: How does a constitution differ from an ordinary criminal or civil law passed by Parliament?
questions.a: An ordinary law regulates daily social conduct and can be changed by Parliament through a regular legislative majority, whereas a constitution sets the rules for how laws are made and requires a special, harder amendment process to change. A wrong answer shows a failure to grasp the foundational versus operational nature of legal documents.

questions.q: Evaluate this statement: "A constitution is only needed in democracies because dictatorships do not have rules." Is this accurate?
questions.a: This is inaccurate; even dictatorships or monarchies often have constitutions or decrees that structure their governance, but a *democratic* constitution specifically limits state power and protects citizen rights. A wrong answer reveals a misunderstanding that any rulebook is automatically a democratic constitution.

questions.q: Design a simple rule or clause that you would include in a new school constitution to ensure fairness and prevent any single student council member from having absolute power.
questions.a: A successful answer will establish a check-and-balance mechanism, such as requiring approval from both a student committee and a teacher representative before a school rule is enacted. A poor answer gives all power to one person or lacks any structural protection against abuse.
